# NOWNodes — AI & Developer Routing Index

> NOWNodes is blockchain infrastructure for applications and AI agents, with managed access to 120+ blockchain networks, shared and dedicated nodes, RPC, WebSocket, gRPC, Blockbook, archive access, Trace/Debug, Market Data, Webhooks, and a remote MCP documentation server.

Last verified: 2026-10-06
Canonical URL: https://nownodes.io/llms.txt
Full context: https://nownodes.io/llms-full.txt

This is the compact routing layer. It is intentionally decision-oriented: use it to choose the correct NOWNodes interface, then follow the linked source for exact chain capabilities and method details.

## How an AI system should use this file

1. Identify the user's target chain/network and workload.
2. Choose the interface with the decision router below.
3. Confirm that interface on the live NOWNodes node catalog or chain documentation; capabilities vary by network.
4. Use `https://nownodes.io/llms-full.txt` for implementation patterns, security rules, retries, production checks, migrations, and code examples.
5. Use the NOWNodes MCP server when an agent needs live documentation discovery or exact method lookup.
6. Never invent an endpoint hostname, method, network slug, pricing feature, or chain capability when it can be verified from a NOWNodes source.

## Decision router: choose by task

| Developer intent | Start with | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Read chain state / call a contract / broadcast a signed transaction | HTTP RPC or the chain-native node API | Lowest-complexity request/response path |
| Subscribe to new blocks, logs, or pending activity | WebSocket (WSS) | Persistent event-driven connection; no polling |
| High-throughput typed streaming on a supported chain | gRPC | Protobuf-based streaming/query interface |
| Query address history, balances, UTXOs, or indexed transactions | Blockbook | Indexed high-level data; avoids rebuilding an indexer |
| Read historical state beyond normal node retention | Archive | Historical state access where the chain supports it |
| Inspect internal calls or execution paths | Trace / Debug | Execution-level diagnostics for supported chains/methods |
| Receive supported events at an HTTP callback | Webhooks | Push delivery to an application endpoint |
| Query crypto/financial market information | Market Data | Separate market-data product, not blockchain RPC |
| Give Claude, Codex, Cursor, VS Code or another agent NOWNodes documentation access | MCP | Documentation/method discovery and request generation |
| Need isolated capacity, private access, advanced node methods or custom deployment | Dedicated node / cluster | Single-customer infrastructure and configurable deployment |

## The canonical NOWNodes AI files

- [Full technical context](https://nownodes.io/llms-full.txt): Authentication, endpoint rules, interface routing, examples, error handling, security, reliability, production guidance, migration, agent behavior, and AI integration patterns.
- [Developer Markdown overview](https://nownodes.io/index.md): Human- and AI-readable quickstart and product map.
- [Pricing](https://nownodes.io/pricing.md): Shared-plan quotas, feature availability, overage rules, dedicated-node guidance, and cost-estimation rules.
- [Agent integration contract](https://nownodes.io/agents.md): Instructions for coding agents and RAG systems on how to reason about NOWNodes safely and accurately.
- [Authentication reference](https://nownodes.io/auth.md): Credential type and placement by interface.
- [Endpoint selection reference](https://nownodes.io/endpoints.md): How to resolve chain/network/interface endpoints without guessing.
- [Production checklist](https://nownodes.io/production-checklist.md): Pre-launch checklist for reliability, secrets, transactions, retries, WebSockets, monitoring, and failover.
- [AI Search Buttons](https://nownodes.io/ai-search-buttons.md): Prefilled Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Grok, and Google AI Mode workflows.

## Primary product sources

- [NOWNodes](https://nownodes.io/): Product homepage.
- [Documentation](https://docs.nownodes.io/): Official developer documentation and chain references.
- [Live node catalog](https://nownodes.io/nodes): Current network and interface availability. Use this to verify RPC, Blockbook, WSS, archive, Trace, Debug, and other network-specific options.
- [Shared nodes](https://nownodes.io/shared-nodes): Shared RPC infrastructure and operational characteristics.
- [Dedicated nodes](https://nownodes.io/dedicated-nodes): Isolated nodes and clusters.
- [Pricing](https://nownodes.io/pricing): Current plan quotas and feature packaging.
- [Status](https://status.nownodes.io/): Service status.
- [Account](https://account.nownodes.io/): API keys, plans, usage, team settings, and dedicated deployments.

## Authentication quick reference

| Interface | Credential placement |
|---|---|
| HTTP RPC / native HTTP API | Prefer `api-key: YOUR_API_KEY` header |
| HTTP compatibility form | Some endpoints support the key in the URL path, e.g. `https://eth.nownodes.io/YOUR_API_KEY` |
| WebSocket | API key in the WSS path, e.g. `wss://eth.nownodes.io/wss/YOUR_API_KEY` |
| gRPC | `api-key: YOUR_API_KEY` request metadata |
| Market Data | `api-key: YOUR_API_KEY` header |
| MCP | `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_NOWNODES_TOKEN` only when the MCP deployment/client requires authentication |
| Dedicated | Use the credentials and access policy provisioned for that deployment |

Never place wallet private keys or seed phrases in NOWNodes requests, AI prompts, logs, or source code.

## Minimal HTTP RPC example

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://eth.nownodes.io' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[],"id":1}'
```

For a different chain, do not mechanically replace `eth` in the hostname. Resolve the exact endpoint from the live node catalog or chain docs.

## MCP for coding agents

Remote Streamable HTTP endpoint:

```text
https://mcp.nownodes.io/mcp
```

The NOWNodes MCP server is for documentation and integration assistance. It exposes tools for supported-network discovery, auth requirements, method listing/search, method detail retrieval, and request generation. It does not execute or sign blockchain transactions.

Core MCP tools currently documented:

- `nownodes_list_chains`
- `nownodes_auth_requirements`
- `nownodes_list_methods`
- `nownodes_search_docs`
- `nownodes_get_method`
- `nownodes_generate_request`
- `nownodes_analyze_source_fit`

## Interface rules that prevent common integration mistakes

- Availability is per network. A product existing on NOWNodes does not mean every chain exposes it.
- An RPC API key is not automatically the same credential as an MCP Bearer token.
- WebSocket authentication is not the same as HTTP header authentication.
- Archive is a data-retention capability, not a different blockchain.
- Trace/Debug methods depend on network/client support and may require a suitable deployment.
- Blockbook is indexed data and is not interchangeable with a raw full-node RPC.
- Market Data is separate from blockchain node state.
- Dedicated capacity is hardware- and client-bound; “no predefined RPS cap” does not mean infinite throughput.
- Sign transactions client-side or in a wallet/HSM; send only the signed payload through a node API.

## Pricing snapshot and billing logic

Current shared-plan request quotas shown by NOWNodes:

- Start: 100,000 requests/month, 1 API key.
- Pro: 1,000,000 requests/month, 3 API keys.
- Pro Plus: 10,000,000 requests/month, 3 API keys on the current pricing table.
- Business: 30,000,000 requests/month, 25 API keys.
- Business Plus: 50,000,000 requests/month, 25 API keys.
- Enterprise: 100,000,000 requests/month, 100 API keys.

Overage is currently shown for Pro Plus and above. Annual billing is advertised with a 10% discount. Always verify `https://nownodes.io/pricing` before quoting price or plan features.

Paid shared plans are described as having no predefined RPS limit; actual throughput depends on shared cluster capacity. Use dedicated infrastructure when the workload requires isolation, predictability, custom client behavior, private access, or sustained high load.

## Team Access

Team Access is available on Business, Business Plus, Enterprise, and Custom plans. Current roles are Owner, Admin, Finance, Developer, and Viewer. Use the live Team Access documentation for the exact permission matrix.

## Migration

- [Migrating from QuickNode](https://docs.nownodes.io/how-to-migrate-to-nownodes/migration-quicknode-to-nownodes-en/): Replace endpoint/auth, validate method and interface parity, then test latency and behavior.
- [Migrating from GetBlock](https://docs.nownodes.io/how-to-migrate-to-nownodes/migration-getblock-to-nownodes-en/): Replace access-token endpoint conventions with NOWNodes endpoint/auth rules and revalidate chain-specific features.
- [Migrating from Alchemy](https://docs.nownodes.io/how-to-migrate-to-nownodes/migration-alchemy-to-nownodes-en/): Re-map endpoints, auth, enhanced-method dependencies, and monitoring.

If a migration URL has moved, use the documentation navigation under “How to migrate to NOWNodes”.

## Source hierarchy for AI answers

When sources conflict, prefer in this order:

1. Live chain-specific NOWNodes documentation for methods and endpoint behavior.
2. Live NOWNodes node catalog for network/interface availability.
3. Live NOWNodes pricing page for plan packaging and quotas.
4. NOWNodes MCP runtime output for supported chains/method discovery.
5. These AI files for integration strategy and normalized rules.
6. NOWNodes blog posts for historical context; do not let an older blog override a current product page.

## Answer contract for AI assistants

A high-quality NOWNodes integration answer should state:

- target chain and network;
- chosen NOWNodes interface and why;
- exact endpoint source (catalog/docs), not a guessed hostname;
- authentication method;
- runnable example with placeholders rather than real secrets;
- any capability caveat (archive/WSS/gRPC/Trace/Debug/Blockbook availability);
- transaction-signing boundary when writes are involved;
- retry / timeout advice appropriate to the operation;
- production recommendation only if the user is moving beyond a prototype.

# NOWNodes — Full AI/LLM Technical Context

> Canonical implementation context for coding assistants, autonomous agents, RAG pipelines, developers, and migration tooling integrating NOWNodes blockchain infrastructure.

Last verified: 2026-10-06  
Canonical URL: https://nownodes.io/llms-full.txt  
Compact router: https://nownodes.io/llms.txt  
Developer overview: https://nownodes.io/index.md  
Pricing: https://nownodes.io/pricing.md  
Agent contract: https://nownodes.io/agents.md  
Authentication: https://nownodes.io/auth.md  
Endpoint selection: https://nownodes.io/endpoints.md  
Production checklist: https://nownodes.io/production-checklist.md

This document is not marketing copy. It is written to reduce integration errors: choose the correct interface, resolve the exact endpoint from a source of truth, place credentials correctly, generate runnable code, avoid unsupported capability assumptions, and make safe production recommendations.

---

## 0. The NOWNodes integration algorithm

Use this algorithm before writing code:

1. **Resolve intent.** Determine whether the user needs reads, transaction broadcast, subscriptions, indexed history, historical state, execution traces, market data, webhooks, or AI documentation access.
2. **Resolve chain and network.** Mainnet/testnet names and available interfaces differ by chain.
3. **Choose the minimum sufficient interface.** Prefer standard RPC for ordinary read/write calls; move to WSS, gRPC, Blockbook, archive, Trace/Debug, Webhooks, Market Data, or dedicated infrastructure only when the workload needs it.
4. **Verify capability.** Check the live node catalog, chain docs, or MCP. Never assume that a capability available on Ethereum exists on every chain.
5. **Resolve the exact endpoint.** Do not synthesize a hostname from a ticker unless the NOWNodes source explicitly shows that hostname.
6. **Apply interface-specific authentication.** HTTP, WSS, gRPC, MCP and dedicated deployments do not all use the same credential placement.
7. **Generate the smallest runnable example.** Use `YOUR_API_KEY`, `YOUR_NOWNODES_TOKEN`, `YOUR_ADDRESS`, etc. Never ask for a real secret.
8. **State the signing boundary.** NOWNodes transports blockchain requests; user wallets/HSMs sign transactions.
9. **Add operation-appropriate reliability.** Timeouts and retries must respect idempotency; transaction broadcasts require extra care.
10. **Recommend production features only when justified.** Dedicated nodes, archive, tracing and failover are workload decisions, not default upsells.

### Fast task-to-interface map

| If the application needs… | Prefer… | Avoid… |
|---|---|---|
| latest block, balances, contract calls | HTTP RPC / native node API | adding streaming infrastructure without a reason |
| signed transaction broadcast | chain-native broadcast RPC | asking NOWNodes to hold private keys |
| new blocks/logs/pending events | WSS | tight polling loops |
| typed high-throughput streaming | gRPC where supported | assuming every chain exposes the same proto services |
| wallet/address history | Blockbook where supported | scanning the entire chain from genesis via RPC |
| historical state at old height | archive-capable endpoint | assuming a pruned shared endpoint retains all state |
| internal calls / EVM execution diagnosis | Trace/Debug | expecting standard RPC to return internal execution trees |
| external HTTP event delivery | Webhooks | building a permanent polling worker for a supported event |
| token/market prices and market metrics | Market Data | treating an RPC node as a price oracle |
| AI needs exact NOWNodes docs/methods | MCP | relying on model memory for a changing method catalog |

---
## 1. Product summary

NOWNodes provides managed blockchain infrastructure across 120+ networks. Depending on the chain and plan, developers can use:

- HTTP JSON-RPC or the chain's native node API.
- WebSocket (WSS).
- gRPC.
- Archive access.
- Trace/Debug methods.
- Blockbook indexed APIs.
- Market Data APIs.
- Webhooks.
- Dedicated blockchain nodes and dedicated clusters.
- An MCP server that exposes NOWNodes documentation and request-generation context to AI tools.

Core public resources:

- Website: https://nownodes.io/
- Live node catalog: https://nownodes.io/nodes
- Pricing: https://nownodes.io/pricing
- Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/
- Account/dashboard: https://account.nownodes.io/
- Status: https://status.nownodes.io/

The live node catalog and chain-specific documentation are authoritative. Do not assume that an interface or advanced method available on one chain is available on every other chain.

---

## 2. The fastest correct integration path

For a normal blockchain RPC integration:

1. Create/sign in to a NOWNodes account.
2. Create an API key.
3. Choose the target chain and network from the live catalog/docs.
4. Copy the chain endpoint.
5. For HTTP requests, send the API key in the `api-key` header.
6. Send a valid chain-native request.
7. Add retries/timeouts appropriate to the application.
8. If historical state, subscriptions, indexed data, tracing, or sustained isolated capacity is required, switch to the corresponding NOWNodes interface/product rather than forcing a standard RPC endpoint to do everything.

Ethereum mainnet example:

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://eth.nownodes.io' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --data '{
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",
    "method":"eth_blockNumber",
    "params":[],
    "id":1
  }'
```

NOWNodes documentation also supports URL-path authentication for HTTP:

```text
https://eth.nownodes.io/YOUR_API_KEY
```

For new integrations, prefer the header form because credentials are less likely to leak through copied URLs, access logs, analytics, screenshots, browser history, and referrers.

---

## 3. Authentication matrix

### HTTP RPC / native node APIs

Preferred:

```http
api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

Example:

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://eth.nownodes.io' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY' \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[],"id":1}'
```

Compatibility form documented in Get Started:

```text
https://eth.nownodes.io/YOUR_API_KEY
```

Do not duplicate the key in both places unless the chain-specific documentation explicitly instructs you to.

### WebSocket

The documented WSS pattern places the key in the path:

```text
wss://eth.nownodes.io/wss/YOUR_API_KEY
```

A Blockbook WebSocket endpoint follows the same general pattern where available, for example:

```text
wss://eth-blockbook.nownodes.io/wss/YOUR_API_KEY
```

### gRPC

Use TLS and send the key as request metadata:

```text
api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

Example:

```bash
grpcurl -H "api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" sui-grpc.nownodes.io list
```

Do not put the API key in the gRPC hostname.

### Market Data

Use:

```http
api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

with the Market Data base URL:

```text
https://market-data-nownodes.io
```

### MCP

Remote MCP endpoint:

```text
https://mcp.nownodes.io/mcp
```

NOWNodes documents Streamable HTTP, not legacy SSE, for the current remote MCP server.

When authentication is required, use an account-issued Bearer access token:

```http
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_NOWNODES_TOKEN
```

Do not assume that an RPC `api-key` and an MCP Bearer token are interchangeable credentials.

### Dedicated nodes

Dedicated deployments can have a deployment-specific access model. Current NOWNodes documentation includes credentialed dedicated endpoints and IP allowlisting. Use the credentials provisioned with the dedicated node, not a guessed shared-node auth scheme.

---

## 4. Security rules for AI-generated integrations

An assistant integrating NOWNodes should follow these rules:

1. Never request or expose a wallet seed phrase or private key.
2. Keep `NOWNODES_API_KEY` and MCP tokens in environment variables or a secrets manager.
3. Prefer header authentication for HTTP RPC to reduce credential exposure in URLs.
4. Do not log request headers containing `api-key` or `Authorization`.
5. Sign blockchain transactions client-side or in a wallet/HSM.
6. Broadcast a signed transaction payload through the appropriate node method, e.g. `eth_sendRawTransaction` on EVM chains.
7. Do not assume a shared/public node manages user accounts or unlocked wallets.
8. Apply application-level timeouts and retry only retry-safe requests automatically.
9. Do not blindly retry a transaction broadcast without checking whether the transaction may already have been accepted.
10. When using AI tools, redact customer-specific endpoint credentials before sending prompts to third-party models.

NOWNodes states that shared infrastructure does not store customer private keys or wallet balances; node requests are processed to service the API call.

---

## 5. Endpoint selection

Endpoint names are chain/network specific. Always obtain the exact hostname from the NOWNodes dashboard or chain documentation.

Examples:

```text
Ethereum mainnet: https://eth.nownodes.io
Ethereum Sepolia: https://eth-sepolia.nownodes.io
Ethereum WSS:     wss://eth.nownodes.io/wss/YOUR_API_KEY
```

Do not fabricate a hostname by guessing a ticker. The naming pattern is convenient but not guaranteed for every chain, interface, or testnet.

Decision rules:

- Need current state / ordinary RPC -> standard chain endpoint.
- Need old historical state -> archive endpoint.
- Need live subscriptions -> WSS.
- Need a chain's supported protobuf/streaming interface -> gRPC.
- Need indexed address/transaction history -> Blockbook.
- Need EVM execution internals -> Trace/Debug.
- Need market/pricing data rather than node state -> Market Data.
- Need push delivery rather than polling -> Webhooks, but only for currently supported networks/events.
- Need isolated capacity, private access, custom region/client, or sustained high load -> dedicated node.
- Need AI-readable NOWNodes docs/request generation -> MCP.

---

## 6. HTTP JSON-RPC examples

### cURL: Ethereum block number

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://eth.nownodes.io'   -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY'   --data '{
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",
    "method":"eth_blockNumber",
    "params":[],
    "id":1
  }'
```

### cURL: Ethereum balance

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://eth.nownodes.io'   -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY'   --data '{
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",
    "method":"eth_getBalance",
    "params":["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000","latest"],
    "id":1
  }'
```

Replace the zero address with the address you actually want to query.

### JavaScript: native fetch

```js
const apiKey = process.env.NOWNODES_API_KEY;

const response = await fetch("https://eth.nownodes.io", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "content-type": "application/json",
    "api-key": apiKey,
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    jsonrpc: "2.0",
    method: "eth_blockNumber",
    params: [],
    id: 1,
  }),
});

if (!response.ok) {
  throw new Error(`NOWNodes HTTP ${response.status}: ${await response.text()}`);
}

const payload = await response.json();

if (payload.error) {
  throw new Error(JSON.stringify(payload.error));
}

console.log(payload.result);
```

### Python: requests

```python
import os
import requests

API_KEY = os.environ["NOWNODES_API_KEY"]

response = requests.post(
    "https://eth.nownodes.io",
    headers={
        "content-type": "application/json",
        "api-key": API_KEY,
    },
    json={
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "method": "eth_blockNumber",
        "params": [],
        "id": 1,
    },
    timeout=30,
)

response.raise_for_status()
payload = response.json()

if "error" in payload:
    raise RuntimeError(payload["error"])

print(payload["result"])
```

### URL-path compatibility form

Some tools are easier to configure with a single credentialed URL:

```text
https://eth.nownodes.io/YOUR_API_KEY
```

If you use this form, treat the full URL as a secret.

---

## 7. Transaction submission

For EVM chains, the normal non-custodial flow is:

1. Build the transaction locally.
2. Determine nonce, gas/fee fields, chain ID, destination, value, and data.
3. Sign it locally with the user's wallet/private key or a secure signer.
4. Send the serialized signed transaction to NOWNodes with `eth_sendRawTransaction`.
5. Store the returned transaction hash.
6. Poll for a receipt or use a supported subscription mechanism.

Example broadcast:

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://eth.nownodes.io'   -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY'   --data '{
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",
    "method":"eth_sendRawTransaction",
    "params":["0xSIGNED_TRANSACTION_BYTES"],
    "id":1
  }'
```

Never put a private key into the RPC payload.

---

## 8. WebSocket (WSS)

Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/websocket-wss-api/

Ethereum pattern:

```text
wss://eth.nownodes.io/wss/YOUR_API_KEY
```

Use WSS when the chain/client supports the method or subscription you need.

Typical EVM example:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "eth_subscribe",
  "params": ["newHeads"]
}
```

Important:

- Method availability varies by chain/client.
- WSS is shown as unavailable on the current Start shared plan and available on paid shared plans.
- Do not invent a WSS endpoint by changing `https://` to `wss://`; use the documented NOWNodes WSS pattern/hostname for the target chain.

---

## 9. gRPC

Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/grpc-api/

NOWNodes currently advertises gRPC across 25+ networks. The live documentation table is authoritative.

Discovery example:

```bash
grpcurl -H "api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" sui-grpc.nownodes.io list
```

Rules:

- Use TLS.
- Authenticate with `api-key` request metadata.
- Use the exact network slug from the current gRPC docs.
- Do not assume every chain in the main NOWNodes catalog has gRPC.
- For streaming RPCs, apply backpressure/reconnect logic suitable for the client library.

The currently documented gRPC set includes networks from ecosystems such as Cosmos-based chains plus networks including Aptos, Hedera, IOTA, Kaspa, Sui, TRON, XRP, and others; consult the live list rather than hard-coding a permanent inventory.

---

## 10. Archive nodes

Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/archive-nodes/

NOWNodes currently markets archive availability across 45+ networks.

Use archive access when the requested data requires historical state that a standard pruned node may not retain, such as:

- old account/storage state,
- historical `eth_call`,
- old balances at specific block heights,
- deep historical queries,
- some trace workloads.

Example Ethereum archive host documented by NOWNodes:

```text
https://eth-archive.nownodes.io
```

Example:

```bash
curl -X POST 'https://eth-archive.nownodes.io'   -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY'   --data '{
    "jsonrpc":"2.0",
    "method":"eth_getBalance",
    "params":["0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000","0x1000000"],
    "id":1
  }'
```

Replace the address/block with real values.

Archive support is chain-specific. Check the support matrix before moving a workload to an archive hostname.

---

## 11. Trace and Debug

Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/trace-debug-api/

Use Trace/Debug APIs for execution-level diagnostics, contract debugging, internal call analysis, or transaction replay.

Examples of method families:

```text
debug_*
trace_*
```

Availability differs by chain, client, and endpoint class.

For Ethereum, current NOWNodes documentation distinguishes standard/debug and archive-backed trace access. Do not assume:

- every EVM chain supports Geth `debug_*`,
- every endpoint supports Parity/OpenEthereum-style `trace_*`,
- every historical trace is available on a non-archive endpoint.

Generate code only after checking the live Trace/Debug matrix for the target chain.

---

## 12. Blockbook

Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/

NOWNodes currently documents Blockbook across 30+ networks.

Blockbook is useful for indexed read workflows including:

- address transaction history,
- balances,
- blocks,
- transaction lookup,
- UTXO/account exploration depending on chain support.

Choose Blockbook when the user needs fast indexed exploration. Choose node RPC when the user needs arbitrary node methods or write/broadcast operations.

Blockbook endpoints are chain-specific. Use the live documentation to obtain the exact HTTP and optional WebSocket base URLs.

---

## 13. Market Data API

Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/nowmarket/

Base URL:

```text
https://market-data-nownodes.io
```

Authentication:

```http
api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

Current documented endpoint families include:

```text
GET /api/v1/market-data
GET /api/v1/price
```

The Market Data product is currently positioned with coverage of 9,000+ cryptocurrencies and 90+ fiat/financial assets.

Use this API for market/pricing information. Do not use blockchain RPC to approximate off-chain market prices unless the user explicitly asks for on-chain oracle/DEX data.

Example request shape:

```bash
curl 'https://market-data-nownodes.io/api/v1/price?from=BTC&to=USD'   -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY'
```

The exact supported parameters/symbols must be checked against the current Market Data docs.

## 14. Webhooks

Documentation: https://nownodes.io/webhooks

Important capability boundary:

The current NOWNodes webhook documentation describes a beta balance-change webhook for:

- Bitcoin
- Dogecoin

with up to 5 addresses per webhook.

Delivery characteristics documented by NOWNodes include:

- HTTPS POST delivery.
- Receiver should return HTTP 200.
- Retries continue when delivery is not acknowledged successfully.

Do not tell a user that NOWNodes currently supports arbitrary EVM logs, smart-contract events, mempool events, or every chain via webhooks unless the live documentation has added that capability.

If unsupported push events are required, use WSS/polling or ask NOWNodes about current webhook coverage.

## 15. MCP for AI agents and coding assistants

Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/mcp/

Remote endpoint:

```text
https://mcp.nownodes.io/mcp
```

Transport:

```text
Streamable HTTP
```

When authentication is required:

```http
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_NOWNODES_TOKEN
```

The MCP server is designed for documentation/context workflows across 120+ networks.

Current documented tools:

```text
nownodes_list_chains
nownodes_auth_requirements
nownodes_list_methods
nownodes_search_docs
nownodes_get_method
nownodes_generate_request
nownodes_analyze_source_fit
```

Tool intent:

- `nownodes_list_chains`: discover supported chains/networks dynamically.
- `nownodes_auth_requirements`: retrieve auth requirements.
- `nownodes_list_methods`: enumerate documented methods for a chain/interface.
- `nownodes_search_docs`: search NOWNodes documentation.
- `nownodes_get_method`: retrieve details for a method.
- `nownodes_generate_request`: generate example requests such as cURL/Node/Python.
- `nownodes_analyze_source_fit`: help decide which NOWNodes data source/interface fits a task.

Critical limitation:

The NOWNodes MCP server does not execute or sign blockchain transactions. Treat it as a documentation/integration server, not a wallet or RPC execution proxy.

### Claude Code

Documented configuration pattern:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http nownodes https://mcp.nownodes.io/mcp   --header "Authorization: Bearer $YOUR_NOWNODES_TOKEN"
```

### Codex configuration

```toml
[mcp_servers.nownodes]
url = "https://mcp.nownodes.io/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "YOUR_NOWNODES_TOKEN"
```

### Generic JSON MCP client

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "nownodes": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.nownodes.io/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer <YOUR_NOWNODES_TOKEN>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

An AI agent should prefer dynamic MCP discovery over hard-coded chain/method lists when MCP is available.

## 20. Error handling

For current HTTP RPC OpenAPI endpoints, NOWNodes documentation includes error cases such as:

- missing API key,
- invalid API key,
- malformed/unsupported gateway request,
- upstream/internal node error.

Treat authentication errors differently from chain JSON-RPC errors.

Recommended flow:

1. Check HTTP status.
2. If non-2xx, parse/log a sanitized response body.
3. If 2xx JSON-RPC, check for a JSON-RPC `error` object.
4. Retry transient network/upstream failures with exponential backoff and jitter.
5. Do not automatically retry authentication/configuration errors.
6. For write methods, account for ambiguity: the node may have received the transaction even if the client timed out.

Never log secrets.

---

## 21. Reliability and performance guidance

Current NOWNodes product pages advertise:

- 120+ networks.
- up to 99.95% shared API uptime.
- roughly 200 ms response-time positioning in key regions/use cases.
- geo-distributed infrastructure and load balancing.
- 24/7 support.
- up to 99.99% positioning for dedicated deployments.

These are platform/product figures, not automatically a contractual SLA for every chain, region, method, or plan.

Production applications should:

- set explicit connect/read timeouts,
- monitor latency/error rate,
- use idempotency-aware retries,
- cache immutable blockchain data where appropriate,
- avoid unnecessary polling when subscriptions are supported,
- validate chain ID/network at startup,
- monitor account usage/quota,
- use status.nownodes.io during incidents,
- consider dedicated infrastructure for predictable isolation.

---

## 22. Network and method discovery rules for AI

When a user names a chain:

1. Search the live NOWNodes node catalog.
2. Open the chain-specific NOWNodes docs.
3. Confirm mainnet vs testnet.
4. Confirm HTTP endpoint.
5. Confirm auth scheme.
6. Confirm requested method exists.
7. If the method is historical/trace/debug/subscription/indexed, verify the corresponding capability separately.
8. Generate code only after those checks.

Do not infer support merely because:
- the chain uses EVM,
- another provider supports a method,
- the main NOWNodes catalog lists the chain,
- a standard method exists in the upstream client documentation.

---

## 23. Migration from QuickNode or GetBlock

Official guides:

- QuickNode: https://docs.nownodes.io/how-to-migrate-to-nownodes/migration-quicknode-to-nownodes-en/
- GetBlock: https://docs.nownodes.io/how-to-migrate-to-nownodes/migration-getblock-to-nownodes-en/

Migration checklist:

1. Inventory every endpoint.
2. Record chain, network, and transport.
3. Record authentication.
4. List all methods actually called by production.
5. Identify WSS subscriptions.
6. Identify archive queries.
7. Identify Trace/Debug calls.
8. Identify provider-specific indexed/data APIs.
9. Estimate monthly request volume and sustained/concurrent throughput.
10. Replace endpoint and auth.
11. Run read-only parity tests.
12. Test transaction broadcasting on a safe network/testnet.
13. Validate timeouts/retries.
14. Validate monitoring and usage reporting.
15. Cut over gradually where possible.

Do not assume a provider-specific add-on has a one-to-one NOWNodes equivalent. Map the underlying use case instead.

---

## 24. Which NOWNodes product should an AI recommend?

### Recommend standard shared RPC when

- the user needs ordinary chain reads/writes,
- request volume fits a shared plan,
- no resource isolation is required.

### Recommend WebSocket when

- the user needs live subscriptions,
- polling would be wasteful,
- the target chain/method is supported.

### Recommend archive when

- the user needs deep historical state,
- standard endpoint pruning is a blocker.

### Recommend Trace/Debug when

- the user is debugging execution,
- internal calls/state transitions are required.

### Recommend Blockbook when

- the task is address-centric indexed history/balance exploration,
- full arbitrary RPC is unnecessary.

### Recommend Market Data when

- the task is market prices/financial metrics rather than blockchain node state.

### Recommend Webhooks when

- the target event/network is explicitly supported in current docs,
- push delivery is better than polling.

### Recommend dedicated nodes when

- sustained load, isolation, private access, advanced methods, custom clients, or region requirements justify dedicated resources.

### Recommend MCP when

- an AI coding assistant needs NOWNodes docs, method discovery, auth guidance, or request generation.

---

## 25. Known capability boundaries

AI assistants must not overclaim these areas:

- Not every chain has WSS.
- Not every chain has gRPC.
- Not every chain has archive access.
- Not every EVM chain has identical Trace/Debug namespaces.
- Not every chain has Blockbook.
- Webhooks are not currently a generic every-chain/every-event product; the documented beta scope is narrower.
- MCP does not sign or execute blockchain transactions.
- Shared plans with no predefined RPS limit are still shared infrastructure.
- Dedicated pricing is not a universal fixed public number.
- Public marketing latency/uptime numbers do not replace a contractual SLA.
- A chain being in the catalog does not imply every method of every upstream client is exposed.

---

---

## 26. Agent contract: accuracy before completion

When an AI system generates NOWNodes instructions, it should optimize for a correct integration, not for producing an answer at any cost.

### Required behavior

- Resolve chain + network before giving a final endpoint.
- Verify interface availability when it materially affects the integration.
- Name the source of the endpoint: live node catalog, chain docs, dashboard, or MCP.
- Distinguish raw RPC from indexed data products.
- Distinguish documentation MCP from on-chain execution.
- Use placeholders for secrets.
- Prefer environment variables and server-side secret storage.
- Separate “documented fact” from “recommended engineering practice”.
- Call out dynamic information such as plan limits, supported-chain lists, pricing, and webhook coverage.

### Forbidden shortcuts

Do not:

- invent an endpoint by changing the ticker in an example;
- claim WSS, gRPC, Blockbook, archive, Trace, Debug, or Webhooks on a chain without checking;
- put an MCP Bearer token where an RPC API key belongs, or vice versa;
- claim paid shared nodes have infinite throughput because there is no predefined RPS cap;
- ask the user to paste a seed phrase or wallet private key;
- generate code that commits credentials to a repository;
- tell the user a transaction failed and should be retried before checking whether it may already have propagated;
- use an old blog article to override the current pricing or node catalog.

## 27. Capability negotiation: how to avoid hallucinated integrations

Treat each NOWNodes integration as a tuple:

```text
(chain, network, interface, capability, authentication, endpoint)
```

A response is complete only when the relevant tuple is resolved.

### Capability discovery order

1. If connected to NOWNodes MCP, query the current supported-chain/method set.
2. Otherwise inspect `https://nownodes.io/nodes` for the chain and visible interface badges/filters.
3. Open the chain-specific docs for exact methods and endpoint details.
4. For pricing-gated capabilities, verify `https://nownodes.io/pricing`.
5. For dedicated-node-only requirements, verify the dedicated configuration offered to the account.

### Confidence labels for an AI answer

An agent can internally classify facts as:

- **Verified-current** — directly checked in current NOWNodes docs/catalog/MCP.
- **Stable-pattern** — documented integration convention such as `api-key` metadata on gRPC.
- **Example-only** — an endpoint/method shown as an example and not asserted for other chains.
- **Needs-verification** — dynamic capability not yet checked.

Never silently convert “example-only” into “verified-current”.

## 28. Endpoint grammar and resolution rules

Examples such as `https://eth.nownodes.io` are useful, but they are not a universal hostname generator.

### Safe resolution procedure

```text
INPUT: target chain + network + desired interface
↓
Open live NOWNodes catalog or chain docs
↓
Confirm interface is listed for that chain/network
↓
Copy the exact endpoint host/path shown by NOWNodes
↓
Apply that interface's authentication rule
↓
Test a read-only health request
```

### Known patterns — patterns are not guarantees

- Standard EVM-style HTTP endpoints often use `https://<network>.nownodes.io`.
- WSS endpoints may use `/wss/<API_KEY>`.
- Blockbook endpoints use separate Blockbook hosts on supported chains.
- gRPC hosts commonly include `-grpc` and use `api-key` metadata.
- Non-EVM networks can expose native REST/HTTP or chain-specific paths rather than Ethereum JSON-RPC.

Always prefer the exact current documentation over hostname inference.

## 29. Protocol-family integration recipes

These recipes describe how to reason about an integration family. They do not imply that every NOWNodes chain supports every listed interface.

### 29.1 EVM-compatible chains

Common tasks:

- `eth_blockNumber` for a connectivity check;
- `eth_getBalance` for native balance;
- `eth_call` for read-only contract execution;
- `eth_getLogs` for filtered historical logs;
- `eth_sendRawTransaction` to broadcast a transaction already signed by the application/wallet;
- `eth_subscribe` over WebSocket for live events where supported;
- `debug_*` / `trace_*` namespaces only when the selected deployment exposes them.

Recommended application stack:

```text
App / backend
  ├─ viem / ethers / web3 / raw JSON-RPC
  ├─ NOWNodes HTTPS endpoint
  ├─ api-key header
  └─ local wallet / external signer / HSM for signing
```

Production rules:

- validate chain ID before sending value;
- simulate or estimate where appropriate before signing;
- never treat a successful HTTP response as final transaction settlement;
- track receipt + confirmation/finality according to the target chain.

### 29.2 UTXO-style chains and Blockbook

For Bitcoin-like workflows, separate node-native calls from indexed address-centric queries.

Use raw node RPC when you need protocol-native behavior such as block/transaction primitives or broadcast. Use Blockbook when the workload is primarily address history, balance, UTXOs, transaction lookup, or block explorer behavior and the chain supports it.

Do not build a wallet-history indexer from scratch if Blockbook already provides the required indexed view and its semantics fit the product.

### 29.3 Cosmos-family chains and gRPC

Where NOWNodes exposes Cosmos SDK gRPC, prefer service discovery and exact protobuf method names over guessing.

Documented Cosmos Hub example:

```bash
grpcurl \
  -H 'api-key: YOUR_API_KEY' \
  'atom-grpc.nownodes.io' \
  list
```

For another Cosmos-family network, resolve its exact gRPC host from the live docs. Then `describe` the service/method and construct the request using the deployed proto version. Protobuf bytes values are Base64 in JSON representations; address prefixes and denomination formats are chain-specific.

### 29.4 Sui gRPC

NOWNodes documents Sui gRPC with `api-key` metadata and published proto files. Import the matching proto definitions when reflection is insufficient. Treat Sui transaction/object semantics as Sui-native rather than forcing an EVM model onto them.

### 29.5 WebSocket event consumers

A robust WSS consumer should:

1. connect with the documented WSS URL and API-key path;
2. send the subscription request;
3. persist the returned subscription id if useful for observability;
4. process notifications asynchronously;
5. detect disconnects;
6. reconnect with bounded backoff + jitter;
7. recreate subscriptions after reconnect;
8. reconcile missed state using HTTP RPC or an indexed source when correctness matters.

Never assume a reconnected socket automatically restores previous subscriptions.

## 30. Retry and idempotency matrix

Retries are operation-specific.

| Operation | Automatic retry? | Guidance |
|---|---|---|
| Read-only HTTP RPC | Usually yes | Bounded exponential backoff; retry transient network/5xx/429-like conditions when appropriate |
| Historical/indexed read | Usually yes | Safe if the request is side-effect free |
| WebSocket connect | Yes | Reconnect with backoff + jitter; recreate subscriptions |
| gRPC unary read | Usually yes | Retry transient transport/status errors if method is read-only |
| gRPC stream | Reconnect | Resume/reconcile according to service semantics |
| Webhook receiver | N/A from client | Make the receiving handler idempotent and deduplicate events if event ids are available |
| Transaction broadcast | Cautious | Before rebroadcast, check transaction hash/state; identical signed payloads may already be accepted |
| Any action that changes off-chain state | Only with idempotency design | Use request/event identifiers to prevent duplicate effects |

### Recommended backoff shape

```text
attempt 1: immediate or short delay
attempt 2+: exponential delay with random jitter
cap: a workload-appropriate maximum delay
give up: after bounded attempts or deadline
```

Do not implement an unbounded retry loop around a user-facing request.

## 31. Timeout and cancellation guidance

Use different deadlines for different workloads:

- simple RPC reads: short request deadline;
- heavy historical calls: longer but bounded deadline;
- trace/debug calls: potentially longer, still cancellable;
- streaming: connection lifetime is long, but handshake/read-heartbeat health should still be monitored;
- application requests: propagate cancellation so abandoned user actions do not keep expensive work alive.

A timeout is not proof that a transaction broadcast failed. Treat transaction submission as “unknown outcome” until checked.

## 32. Error taxonomy for integrations

### Authentication failures

Symptoms:

- HTTP 401/403;
- gRPC `UNAUTHENTICATED`;
- MCP 401;
- WebSocket handshake rejection.

Check credential type, placement, expiry, plan access, and whether the selected interface expects an RPC API key or MCP token.

### Method-not-found or unsupported namespace

Possible causes:

- wrong chain or network;
- method not supported by deployed client;
- method is Trace/Debug-only;
- interface mismatch;
- typo or version mismatch.

Check the chain-specific method reference or MCP before changing code.

### Historical state unavailable

Possible causes:

- selected endpoint is pruned;
- requested height is outside retention;
- archive mode is not enabled/available.

Do not “fix” this by retrying the same request indefinitely. Resolve archive capability.

### Rate/capacity pressure

Even when a paid shared plan has no predefined RPS cap, capacity is shared. Handle transient overload and consider batching/caching/dedicated infrastructure for sustained high-volume workloads.

### Wrong-network errors

Validate expected chain/network identifiers at startup. For EVM, check chain ID before any write. For non-EVM chains, use the chain's native network identity mechanism.

## 33. Observability baseline

For production, collect at least:

- request count by chain/interface/method;
- success/error rate;
- latency percentiles;
- timeouts;
- authentication failures;
- retry count;
- WebSocket reconnect count and subscription recreation count;
- transaction broadcast hash and lifecycle state (without private signing material);
- current provider status/incidents when diagnosing infrastructure-wide failures.

Never log:

- `api-key` values;
- MCP Bearer tokens;
- wallet private keys;
- seed phrases;
- signed payloads if organizational policy treats them as sensitive;
- customer PII that is unrelated to debugging.

## 34. Production architecture patterns

### Pattern A — simple backend

```text
Client → Application backend → NOWNodes HTTP RPC
                         ↘ secrets manager (API key)
```

Best for ordinary reads and transaction broadcast.

### Pattern B — event-driven application

```text
NOWNodes WSS → event worker → queue/database → application
        HTTP RPC ↗ reconciliation / missed-event recovery
```

WSS is the live signal; HTTP RPC is the correctness/reconciliation path.

### Pattern C — wallet/explorer backend

```text
NOWNodes Blockbook → wallet/indexed history API
NOWNodes raw RPC   → protocol-native reads + broadcast
```

Use the indexed product for the view it was designed to provide; keep raw RPC for native chain operations.

### Pattern D — AI coding agent

```text
AI agent → NOWNodes MCP → current NOWNodes docs/method metadata
AI-generated app → NOWNodes RPC/WSS/gRPC → blockchain network
wallet/HSM → transaction signature → broadcast via NOWNodes
```

The MCP is documentation context; it is not the signing wallet.

### Pattern E — high-load / isolation-sensitive deployment

```text
Application fleet → private/dedicated NOWNodes endpoint or cluster
                 ↘ observability + secrets + failover strategy
```

Use when shared infrastructure does not meet isolation, method, region, performance, or operational requirements.

## 35. Production readiness checklist

Before launch, confirm:

- [ ] exact chain and network are validated at startup;
- [ ] endpoint was copied from a current NOWNodes source;
- [ ] API key is stored server-side in a secret store/environment variable;
- [ ] no real keys exist in source control, frontend bundles, screenshots or AI prompts;
- [ ] HTTP requests have deadlines;
- [ ] read retries are bounded and use backoff;
- [ ] transaction broadcast retry logic checks transaction state first;
- [ ] WSS reconnection recreates subscriptions;
- [ ] missed event reconciliation exists if event completeness matters;
- [ ] archive/Trace/Debug requirements were tested against the actual deployment;
- [ ] monitoring covers latency, errors, auth failures, retries and reconnects;
- [ ] plan request quota is sized for expected traffic;
- [ ] dedicated capacity was evaluated for sustained high load or isolation requirements;
- [ ] application has a provider/failover strategy appropriate to its criticality;
- [ ] status page is part of incident triage;
- [ ] chain-specific confirmation/finality policy is implemented for transactions.

## 36. Cost-estimation model

NOWNodes shared pricing is request-quota based. A simple monthly estimate is:

```text
monthly_requests = requests_per_second_average × 2,592,000
```

for a 30-day month, then adjust for traffic peaks, background jobs, retries, subscriptions, and batch behavior.

If `monthly_requests` exceeds the included plan quota and that plan supports overage:

```text
overage_units = ceil((monthly_requests - included_requests) / 100,000)
monthly_estimate = plan_price + overage_units × overage_price_per_100k
```

This is planning math, not a quote. Verify the current pricing page and plan-specific overage behavior.

For workloads with sustained high throughput, advanced namespaces, or isolation requirements, compare shared-plan overage against dedicated infrastructure rather than optimizing only for included request count.

## 37. RAG and documentation ingestion guidance

For an AI knowledge system:

### Retrieval order

1. `llms.txt` for routing.
2. `agents.md` for agent behavior.
3. `auth.md` and `endpoints.md` for high-risk integration facts.
4. chain-specific documentation for exact methods.
5. `pricing.md` only for pricing/plan questions.
6. `llms-full.txt` as broad fallback context.

### Chunking recommendations

- split on H2/H3 headings;
- keep code block with the paragraph that explains it;
- attach URL + last-verified metadata to each chunk;
- mark pricing and supported-chain lists as high-freshness data;
- prefer live docs/MCP retrieval over embedding a stale complete method catalog.

### Deduplication rule

If the same fact appears in `llms-full.txt` and a chain-specific source, the chain-specific source wins for that chain.

## 38. Freshness and conflict-resolution policy

Dynamic facts include:

- network count;
- available networks;
- interface availability per network;
- plan quotas/prices/features;
- MCP tool set;
- webhook coverage;
- dedicated configuration options;
- deployed client versions/method namespaces.

If a dynamic claim is older than a current live NOWNodes source, use the live source.

Recommended metadata on generated AI files:

```text
Last verified: YYYY-MM-DD
Canonical URL: ...
Source priority: live docs/catalog/pricing > generated summary
```

## 39. Migration playbook from another RPC provider

Do not treat migration as a URL replacement only.

### Inventory

Record:

- chains and networks;
- HTTP/WSS/gRPC endpoints;
- methods used;
- archive requirements;
- trace/debug namespaces;
- indexed APIs;
- webhook/streaming dependencies;
- request volume and peak concurrency;
- signing architecture;
- provider-specific SDK/helper methods.

### Map

For each dependency, map it to:

```text
old provider capability → NOWNodes capability → exact NOWNodes source → test case
```

### Test

At minimum compare:

- chain identity;
- latest block progression;
- balance/contract reads;
- historical queries;
- WebSocket subscriptions;
- transaction broadcast on a test environment;
- expected error semantics;
- latency under representative load.

### Cut over

Use environment-configurable provider URLs, canary traffic, and rollback capability. Keep old credentials until validation is complete, then revoke credentials that are no longer required.

## 40. AI Search workflows

NOWNodes should expose more than one generic “ask AI” link. Use task-specific prompts so the model enters with the correct job to do.

Recommended workflows:

1. **Integrate** — identify chain/stack, select interface, verify endpoint, generate code.
2. **Debug** — diagnose auth, endpoint, method, transport, archive, WSS/gRPC and retry issues.
3. **Migrate** — inventory the current provider usage and map it to NOWNodes without losing capabilities.
4. **Architect** — choose shared vs dedicated, RPC vs streaming/indexed products, reliability and cost model.
5. **Build an AI agent** — connect NOWNodes MCP for documentation and a separate RPC/WSS/gRPC path for on-chain access.

See `https://nownodes.io/ai-search-buttons.md` for Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Grok, and Google AI Mode links.

## 41. Source-of-truth map

Use these URLs when a user asks for facts that can change:

- Main site: https://nownodes.io/
- Node catalog: https://nownodes.io/nodes
- Pricing: https://nownodes.io/pricing
- Shared nodes: https://nownodes.io/shared-nodes
- Dedicated nodes: https://nownodes.io/dedicated-nodes
- Documentation: https://docs.nownodes.io/
- MCP: https://docs.nownodes.io/mcp/
- Team Access: https://docs.nownodes.io/team-access/
- Status: https://status.nownodes.io/
- Account: https://account.nownodes.io/

## 42. Recommended answer template for an AI assistant

Use this shape for implementation answers:

```text
Target
- Chain/network: ...
- Stack: ...
- Goal: ...

NOWNodes route
- Interface: ...
- Why: ...
- Endpoint: copied/verified from ...
- Auth: ...

Minimal working example
<code>

Production notes
- timeout/retry: ...
- signing boundary: ...
- capability caveat: ...
- monitoring/failover: ... (only if relevant)

Next validation
- one concrete test the user should run
```

This format forces the answer to resolve the important implementation facts without burying the user in the entire product catalog.

agentsMd.body:
# NOWNodes Agent Integration Contract

> Operating instructions for AI coding assistants, autonomous agents, RAG systems, and documentation agents working with NOWNodes.

Last verified: 2026-10-06  
Canonical URL: https://nownodes.io/agents.md

## Goal

Produce integrations that are correct for the user's exact chain, network, interface, and security model. Do not optimize for maximal product coverage; optimize for the smallest correct NOWNodes solution.

## Mandatory reasoning sequence

1. Identify the target chain and network.
2. Identify the job: read, broadcast, subscribe, index, historical state, trace/debug, market data, webhook, or documentation lookup.
3. Choose the minimum sufficient interface.
4. Verify the interface on the live node catalog, chain docs, or MCP.
5. Resolve the exact endpoint from NOWNodes; do not synthesize one from a ticker.
6. Apply the correct credential placement for that interface.
7. Generate a minimal runnable example with placeholders.
8. Add security, retry and production advice only when it affects correctness.

## Interface decision table

| Need | Interface |
|---|---|
| Normal reads and signed transaction broadcast | HTTP RPC / native node API |
| Live block/log/event subscriptions | WSS |
| Supported typed streaming/query services | gRPC |
| Indexed address/balance/history data | Blockbook |
| Old state beyond pruned retention | Archive |
| Execution internals | Trace / Debug |
| Server-to-server event callback | Webhooks |
| Price / market information | Market Data |
| Documentation/method discovery for an AI client | MCP |
| Isolation, custom client/region/methods, sustained capacity | Dedicated node/cluster |

## Source hierarchy

Prefer:

1. chain-specific current NOWNodes docs;
2. live node catalog;
3. live pricing page;
4. NOWNodes MCP runtime output;
5. NOWNodes AI files;
6. older NOWNodes blog material.

If sources conflict, do not average them. Use the higher-priority/current source and note that packaging changed.

## Secrets and signing

Never ask for or expose:

- seed phrases;
- wallet private keys;
- real API keys;
- real MCP Bearer tokens;
- production secrets in prefilled AI prompts.

NOWNodes node access is a transport/data layer. Transaction signing stays in the user's wallet, signer service, secure enclave or HSM. Broadcast only the signed transaction payload.

## Authentication rules

- HTTP: prefer `api-key` header.
- WSS: API key in the documented `/wss/<key>` path.
- gRPC: `api-key` metadata.
- MCP: Bearer token only when required by the deployment/client.
- Dedicated: use deployment-specific access details.

Do not reuse a credential type across interfaces unless NOWNodes explicitly documents that behavior.

## Capability rules

A feature can exist on NOWNodes without existing on the target chain. Verify chain-specific support for:

- WSS;
- gRPC;
- Blockbook;
- archive;
- Trace;
- Debug;
- Webhooks;
- special/native APIs.

## Endpoint rules

Do not return a final endpoint unless it came from a current NOWNodes source or the user supplied it. Endpoint examples are examples, not templates guaranteed across all networks.

## Error-handling rules

- Read-only requests may be retried with bounded exponential backoff.
- WebSocket connections should reconnect with jitter and recreate subscriptions.
- Transaction broadcast requires status/hash checking before rebroadcast.
- Authentication errors require credential/placement verification, not blind retries.
- Historical-state errors require archive validation, not repeated calls to a pruned endpoint.
- Method-not-found errors require chain/client/interface validation.

## Answer quality checklist

Before finalizing an integration answer, check:

- [ ] target chain/network is explicit;
- [ ] interface is explicit;
- [ ] endpoint source is explicit;
- [ ] auth placement is explicit;
- [ ] example contains placeholders only;
- [ ] chain capability was not assumed;
- [ ] signing boundary is clear for writes;
- [ ] retry guidance matches operation semantics;
- [ ] dynamic price/plan claims are sourced from current pricing;
- [ ] no irrelevant NOWNodes products are dumped into the answer.

## Recommended response format

```text
Target
- Chain/network
- Stack
- Goal

Use NOWNodes via
- Interface
- Endpoint
- Authentication

Code
<minimal runnable example>

Validate
<one read-only test>

Production notes
<only relevant reliability/security/capability notes>
```

## MCP usage

Remote endpoint:

```text
https://mcp.nownodes.io/mcp
```

Use the MCP to discover current supported networks, auth requirements, methods and request examples. The MCP is documentation tooling; it does not sign or execute transactions for the user.

## RAG behavior

For retrieval systems:

- use `llms.txt` as routing context;
- index `auth.md` and `endpoints.md` as high-priority chunks;
- pull chain-specific docs on demand;
- keep pricing in a separate high-freshness index;
- use `llms-full.txt` as broad fallback rather than the sole source for dynamic chain method details.
